notes.ar: Modern Standard Arabic in Apple's macOS Arabic style: masdar (verbal noun) for buttons and menu items (إضافة، نسخ، جلب), masculine-singular imperative in instructions (اختر، جرّب), headings and section names with the definite article (الفروع، الوسوم). Git and Jira concepts are translated into Arabic words; only command names (rebase, cherry-pick, revert, git, gh, HEAD), product names and examples stay Latin. Quotation marks are « » and punctuation is Arabic (، ؛ ؟). Full CLDR plural forms (zero, one, two, few, many, other) with the counted noun's case (tamyiz: 3-10 plural, 11-99 accusative singular, 100+ singular). Compact ages: د (minutes), س (hours), ي (days), ش (months), ع (years), directly after the number. Strings are worded to start with an Arabic word, so a Latin name at the start does not make the paragraph left-to-right; the one string that must start with a ref placeholder (the checked-out-in tooltip) gets an RLM (U+200F) first, and stash names (stash@{0}) get an LRM (U+200E) after them so the punctuation that follows does not flip the braces. Parent/child commits are الأب/الابن; Jira's parent ticket is a ticket رئيسية. Checked out = نشط (active). Done is تم for the button and a finished clone, but a done ticket or status is منجز (الإنجاز in Definition of Done and Done statuses). Stash = مخبأ, stash (verb) = تخبئة; pop = تطبيق وحذف (apply and delete); drop = حذف. The compact file counts in the working-tree summary are written as label: number (مجهّز: 2 · معدّل: 3 · جديد: 1) to avoid agreement problems in a narrow line.
notes.de: du-form (informal), as Apple's current macOS German (Dein Mac, Versuche es erneut). Git terms stay English nouns with German articles (der Commit, der Branch, der Stash, der Merge, das Release, das Repository) and verbs are German-ified (committen, stashen). Where git has its own German word it is used: vorgemerkt/vormerken for staged/stage, losgelöst for detached, vor/hinter for ahead/behind, divergiert for diverged, Arbeitsverzeichnis for working tree. Apple's German for the usual things (Sichern, Abbrechen, Im Finder anzeigen, Nach Updates suchen, Weitersuchen, Schlüsselbund, Systemeinstellungen, Programme). A no-break space (U+00A0) goes before … as in Apple's menus (Hinzufügen …). Quotes are „ “. Durations (%lld days/hours/minutes) are dative because they only follow nach/seit (nach 3 Tagen). Compact ages: min, h, d, M, J.
notes.es: Tuteo, as Apple's Spanish does (imperatives like Elige, Añade, Compruébalos; infinitives in tooltips). Apple es (Spain) words for macOS things: Ajustes, Ajustes del Sistema, Aplicaciones, Llavero, Finder, barra lateral, Quitar, Añadir; quoted names in « ». Sentence case. Git nouns that developers say in English stay English and masculine, plural with -s (el commit, los commits; el stash, los stashes; el hash; el worktree; el pull request, los pull requests; el rebase; el cherry-pick; el committer). Spanish words for rama, etiqueta, remoto, fusión/fusionar, clonar, aplicar, preparar, borrador, comprobaciones. Verbs built on English nouns use hacer: hacer commit, hacer stash, hacer fetch, hacer pop. Jira terms follow Jira's Spanish UI where it has one (épica, historia, tarea, subtarea, Por hacer, En curso, Listo) but ticket stays ticket. A name of another part of the app is quoted with its exact translation. Compact ages follow CLDR narrow forms: 5min, 3h, 12d, 4m, 2,5a.
notes.fr: Vous-form, imperative like Apple (Choisissez, Activez); sentence case, never Title Case. French typography: no-break space (U+00A0) before : ; ? ! and inside « », typographic apostrophe ’. Git nouns kept in English with French gender: le commit, le tag, le worktree, le rebase, le cherry-pick, le hash, une pull request, une release, une epic, un ticket. Translated like Pro Git / git / VS Code in French: dépôt, branche, fusion/fusionner, indexer/désindexer (stage/unstage), remisage/remiser (stash), appliquer/dépiler/supprimer (apply/pop/drop), valider (commit as a verb: « Rien à valider »), récupérer (fetch), en avance/en retard (ahead/behind), HEAD détachée, extrait(e) (checked out), pile (stack), surligner/surlignage (highlight), relecture (review), vérifications (checks). A pull request's states are feminine (Ouverte, Fusionnée, Fermée; Brouillon). Jira: version corrigée (fix version), publiée (released), À faire / En cours / Terminé. Compact ages: 5 min, 3 h, 12 j, 4 mois, 2,5 a (no-break space). Menu names: Réglages, Réglages Système, le Finder, le Terminal, Rechercher suivant.
notes.hi: आप-form with polite imperatives (-ें/-एँ), as in Apple's Hindi; sentences end with '।'. git and Jira terms are Devanagari transliterations (कमिट, ब्रांच, पुल रिक्वेस्ट, टिकट); Latin stays for Vibe GitTree, GitHub, Jira, git, gh, HEAD, Mac, Finder. macOS words: टर्मिनल, सेटिंग, सिस्टम सेटिंग, ऐप्लिकेशन, कीचेन, रद्द करें, ठीक, पूर्ण, सहेजें, हटाएँ, ख़ारिज करें. Loanword nouns don't change with the count (5 कमिट, 3 टिकट); only फ़ाइल/फ़ाइलें and दिन में/दिनों में do. रिपॉज़िटरी, ब्रांच, पुल रिक्वेस्ट are feminine; कमिट, टैग, टिकट, रिलीज़, स्टैश masculine; labels use invariant words where possible (स्टेज्ड, अनस्टेज्ड, ओपन, बंद). 'X of Y' is written X/Y as Apple does. Progress text: 'X किया जा रहा है…'. Compact ages with no space: मि॰ घं॰ दिन माह वर्ष. Durations used before a postposition (बाद, से) use the oblique घंटे for 1 and many.
notes.id: Formal 'Anda' (capital A), as Apple's Indonesian software. Git terms stay English (commit, branch, tag, remote, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, fetch, clone, stash, pop, drop, stage, unstage, checkout, worktree, diff, hash, HEAD, pull request, check, stack, revert, parent/child), with Indonesian passive 'di-' (di-commit, di-merge, di-stage, di-clone, di-checkout, di-review, di-force-push) and 'Melakukan X…' for progress lines (Melakukan commit…, Melakukan fetch…); only 'apply' is translated (Terapkan). Everyday words as macOS: berkas (file), folder, tautan (link), bar samping (sidebar), bar alat (toolbar), Rantai Kunci (keychain), Pengaturan (Settings), Pengaturan Sistem (System Settings), Aplikasi, Batalkan, Selesai, Hapus, Salin, Tampilkan di Finder, Buka di Terminal, Temukan (Find). Menus, buttons and titles use Indonesian Title Case with lowercase di/ke/dari/dan/yang/untuk/dengan/atau/oleh/sebagai/dalam; sentences and tooltips use sentence case. Ahead/behind: lebih maju / tertinggal; up to date: mutakhir. Jira: tiket, epic/story/task/sub-task stay English, versi perbaikan (fix version), tiket induk (parent ticket), kunci tiket (ticket key), Definition of Done stays English. Compact ages: mnt, j, hr, bln, thn (e.g. 5mnt, 3j, 12hr, 4bln, 2.5thn). Plurals: Indonesian has a single form, so counted strings are plain.
notes.it: Informal tu, as in Apple's Italian: imperatives for commands (Scegli, Apri, Aggiungi), 'fai clic'. Sentence case everywhere; quotes “ ” and the apostrophe ’ as in macOS Italian. Git terms stay English as invariable nouns with Italian articles (il commit, il branch, il repository, lo stash, il tag, il merge, la pull request, la epic, lo stack). 'In checkout', 'in staging' and 'non committato' work as adjectives; 'committare' is not used (say 'eseguire il commit'). Pull request states agree with 'la pull request': aperta, chiusa, unita (merged), bozza. Jira: Da fare, In corso, Completato; Definition of Done stays English. Compact ages: min, h, g, mese/mesi, a.
notes.ja: Polite です/ます in sentences; dictionary form or a noun phrase for buttons, menu items and tooltips (コピー, 開く…); a final 。 only where the English has a final period. macOS wording: ウインドウ, フォルダ, 設定, キャンセル, ターミナル, キーチェーン, アップデート, システム設定. git terms are the katakana developers use. Jira terms follow Jira's Japanese UI: 課題 for ticket (never チケット), エピック, 修正バージョン, 完了の定義, 進行中, 完了; To Do stays English. Working tree = 作業ツリー, linked worktree = ワークツリー. Drop (stash) = 破棄, Remove/Delete = 削除. Counters: bare katakana noun after the number (12コミット, 3ブランチ, 5タグ, 2マージ), 件 for tickets/changes/matches, 個 for files and repositories, 人 for authors; compact ages 5分, 3時間, 12日, 4か月, 2.5年. Names in 「」; ASCII ': ' after labels; full-width （） around Japanese text, ASCII () around shortcuts like (⌘G). No spaces between Japanese and placeholders.
notes.ko: Polite formal register as in Apple's Korean software: statements end in -습니다, instructions in -하세요, short labels, menu items and tooltips are noun phrases or -하기 (복사, 열기, 보기). Git terms that are coinages stay transliterated (커밋, 브랜치, 태그, 스태시, 리베이스, 체리픽, 리버트, 페치, 푸시, 풀 리퀘스트, 워크트리, 체크아웃), while merge, clone and repository follow git's, Xcode's and Microsoft's Korean (병합, 복제, 저장소); Jira terms follow Jira's Korean (에픽, 스토리, 작업, 하위 작업, 수정 버전, 해야 할 일, 진행 중, 완료). Placeholders never take a 받침-dependent particle (은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 와/과, 으로/로): put a fixed noun after them (%@ 브랜치가, %@ 커밋이, %@ 프로젝트의) or use 에, 에서, 의, 보다, 만, or a colon. People in the pull request timeline get 님이 (%@님이 병합했습니다); when a sentence mentions the app (Vibe GitTree) a vowel-ending particle is fine. Counts: noun then number with 개 (커밋 %lld개, 티켓 %lld개), 명 for people; Korean has no plural forms, so plain strings. Compact ages: 분, 시간, 일, 개월, 년. Quotes: curly double quotes. Window is 윈도우 and Terminal 터미널, Finder stays Finder, System Settings is 시스템 설정, Applications is 응용 프로그램, keychain is 키체인, toolbar is 도구 막대. Strings that mention another part of the app use that part's translation (설정 › Jira, 커밋 및 스태시 허용, 커밋하지 않은 변경 사항).
notes.ms: Malay (Malaysia), formal-neutral register: 'anda' for you, as in Apple's Malay. Menus, buttons and titles use Title Case with lower-case function words (dan, dalam, di, ke, pada, untuk, daripada, dengan, yang, oleh, sebagai), like macOS's Malay; sentences and tooltips use sentence case. Git terms stay English as Malaysian developers say them (commit, branch, tag, remote, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, fetch, clone, stash, stage, checkout, worktree, working tree, pull request, hash, upstream, HEAD) and have no plural marking; generic words are Malay (repositori, fail, folder, perubahan, tiket, keluaran, semakan, pemeriksaan). An English git verb that needs a passive or negative takes 'di-' / 'belum' ('di-commit', 'di-merge', 'di-clone', 'di-checkout', 'belum di-commit'; the adjectives 'staged' and 'belum staged' stay as they are); progress lines use 'Sedang <verb>…' for English verbs (Sedang fetch…). Jira has no Malay interface, so Jira's own words stay English (epic, story, task, sub-task, fix version, and status names such as Done/Released) while the app's labels around them are Malay. 'regular expression' stays English. Compact ages: min, j (jam), h (hari), bln, thn. Quotes are “ ”.
notes.nl: Informal je/jouw, as Apple's Dutch software does. Menu items and buttons are imperatives in sentence case, like macOS (Kopieer, Toon, Annuleer, Bewaar, Verwijder…, Gereed, Zoek naar updates…); progress lines are infinitives (Tickets laden…). Git, GitHub and Jira nouns stay English with Dutch articles (de commit, de branch, de stash, de worktree, de pull request); their verbs take Dutch endings (committen, mergen, fetchen, stashen, stagen, unstagen, poppen, droppen; participles gecommit, gemerged, gestaged, gedropt) and the bare stem is the button (Commit, Stash, Fetch, Pop, Drop, Stage). Compounds are one word with Dutch parts (branchnaam, commitbericht, releasedatum, ticketstatus) and hyphenated after a proper name or abbreviation (Jira-profiel, API-token, git-repository, GitHub-repository). Parent and Child stay English because 'ouder' also reads as 'older'. Compact ages: min, u, d, mnd, jr. Quotation marks are curly double quotes.
notes.pl: Apple's Polish style: imperative 2nd person singular for actions (Wybierz, Dodaj, Sprawdź), sentence case for buttons, menus and titles, quoted names in „ ” (U+201E/U+201D). macOS words: Ustawienia, Ustawienia systemowe, Zachowaj (Save), Anuluj, Gotowe, Usuń, Pokaż w Finderze, Otwórz w Terminalu, pasek boczny, pęk kluczy, folder Programy, E-mail. Product names (GitHub, Jira, Xcode) are never inflected: 'na GitHub', 'w Jira', 'z Jira'. Git nouns that Polish developers say in English stay English and take Polish endings: commit (commita, commicie, commity, commitów), stash (stasha, stashe), tag (tagi, tagów), pull request (pull requesty, pull requestów), hash, committer, worktree (worktree'y, worktree'ów), rebase, cherry-pick, revert. Polish words for the rest: repozytorium, gałąź, scalenie/scalony, zdalne, klonuj, zastosuj, usuń. The verb commit is 'zatwierdź' (zatwierdza, Zatwierdzanie…, niezatwierdzone), the noun stays 'commit'; stash as a verb is 'schowaj'. Staging uses git's own word 'indeks': dodaj do indeksu / wyjmij z indeksu / w indeksie / poza indeksem (short header links: Dodaj wszystko / Wyjmij wszystko). Durations are genitive (po upływie 3 dni, od 5 godzin). Compact ages use a no-break space: 5 min, 3 h, 12 d, 4 mies., 2,5 l. Jira terms follow Jira's Polish UI (zgłoszenie, epik, historia, zadanie, podzadanie, Do zrobienia, W toku, Gotowe, wydanie); a ticket is 'zgłoszenie'. Counts needing a noun use one/few/many forms; where a count phrase is inserted with %@ it is nominative, so wording avoids a preposition right before it (e.g. '8 zgłoszeń, w tym 5 gotowych'). A name of another part of the app is used with its exact translation (often in quotes).
notes.pt-BR: Address the user as 'você' (imperative: Escolha, Selecione, Instale); menu items, buttons and tooltips use the infinitive (Copiar, Mostrar, Abrir), progress lines the gerund (Carregando…). Sentence case (only the first word and proper names capitalized), as the brief asks, although Apple's own macOS pt-BR menus use Title Case. Git nouns stay English with Portuguese articles and verbs: o commit, o branch, o stash, o merge, o rebase, o fetch, o remote, o pull request, o HEAD; a tag, a worktree; verbs are 'fazer commit', 'fazer stash', 'fazer fetch', 'fazer pop'. 'Merged' states use 'mesclado' (git's own pt_BR word). stage = 'preparar' (git pt_BR), staged = 'preparado', unstage = 'remover da preparação'; drop = 'descartar'; detached HEAD = 'HEAD desanexado'; checked out = 'com checkout'. Jira terms follow Jira pt-BR: épico, história, tarefa, subtarefa, A fazer, Em andamento, Concluído; 'ticket' stays; Jira/git 'release' = 'lançamento', but the app's own GitHub releases are 'versão'. Settings = 'Ajustes' (macOS pt-BR), System Settings = 'Ajustes do Sistema', keychain = 'chaveiro', Applications = 'Aplicativos', sign in = 'entrar'; 'Verificar' for checking updates and checks, 'Buscar' only for Find. Compact ages: min, h, d, m (month), a (year).
notes.ru: Formal «вы»: polite plural imperatives in sentences (Выберите…), infinitives on menu items, buttons and tooltips (Показать…). Sentence case, « » quotes, ё is written (удалённый, отсоединён). macOS names: Finder, Терминал, Системные настройки, Связка ключей, Программы, боковое меню, панель инструментов. Git nouns are Cyrillic and decline (коммит, тег, хеш, стэш, пулл-реквест, тикет, эпик); command names with no settled Russian word stay Latin and act as indeclinable nouns (fetch, cherry-pick, revert, force-push: «выполните fetch»). Developer usage over bookish forms: «закоммитить» (not «зафиксировать»), «пулл-реквест» (not «запрос на слияние»), «ревью», «стэш» (not «припрятанные изменения»). Index words for staging: «добавить в индекс» / «исключить из индекса», «В индексе» / «Не в индексе». Stash: noun «стэш», verb «отложить в стэш»; pop = «извлечь» (as from a stack), apply = «применить», drop = «удалить». Ahead/behind follow git's Russian output: «опережает … на N», «отстаёт от … на N». Jira terms follow Jira's Russian UI (Эпик, История, Задача, Подзадача, К выполнению, В работе, Готово); a Jira ticket is «тикет» so it never clashes with the issue type «задача». Pull request states and events are masculine (Открыт, Закрыт, Слит, Одобрен) with «пользователем X» for the actor, «от X» after noun phrases (Ревью от X). The sidebar's Remotes section counts remote branches, so it reads «Удалённые ветки». Counts that the app formats first ("N tickets", "N commits") are inserted after «всего», never after «из», because those phrases are nominative. Compact ages use a no-break space: 5 мин, 3 ч, 12 дн, 4 мес, 2.5 г. Durations are accusative after «через» (через 1 минуту).
notes.th: Neutral polite register (no ครับ/ค่ะ, almost no คุณ), like Apple's Thai UI. Git and Jira terms are written in Thai script as loanwords (คอมมิต, แบรนช์, เมิร์จ, ทิกเก็ต), never mixed with Latin; Latin stays only for names, commands and HEAD. No full stop at the end of a sentence and no question mark (questions end in หรือไม่); sentences inside one string are separated by a space. ไม้ยมก is attached (อื่นๆ). A space separates Thai text from numbers and %@ placeholders. Compact ages: น. ชม. วัน ด. ปี. parent commit = คอมมิตก่อนหน้า, child commit = คอมมิตถัดไป, working tree = โฟลเดอร์ทำงาน (not the same word as worktree = เวิร์กทรี), stack of pull requests = ซ้อนกัน (avoids สแตก, which is one letter from สแตช).
notes.tr: Formal siz-form as in Apple's Turkish: bare imperative on buttons, menu items and tooltips (Kopyala, Aç), polite plural imperative in sentences (seçin, yükleyin). Title Case in menus, buttons and titles as macOS Turkish does; sentence case elsewhere. Git jargon developers say in English stays English with Turkish suffixes after an apostrophe that follow the pronunciation (commit’ler, ticket’ler, stash’i, stage’e, pull request’i, worktree’de, hash’i); words with an established Turkish form are translated (depo, dal, etiket, uzak depo, birleştirme, klonla, ebeveyn). Plural nouns after a number stay singular (3 commit, 5 dosya). Typographic apostrophe ’ before suffixes, curly quotes “ ”. Never put a suffix on a placeholder (its ending is unknown): use a free word after it (üzerinde, tarafından, ile, sonra). Checkout is kept: checkout edilmiş. Release notes: Sürüm Notları. Compact ages follow CLDR narrow units: dk, sa, g, ay, y.
notes.uk: Polite plural "ви" (imperative: Виберіть, Установіть; infinitives on buttons and menus: Скасувати, Скопіювати, Показати у Finder). Sentence case; « » for quoted names; typographic apostrophe ’ (рев’ю, зв’язка). macOS words: Параметри (Settings), Параметри системи (System Settings), Термінал, Finder, зв’язка ключів, Програми. Common git nouns are Cyrillic (коміт, гілка, тег, злиття, перебазування, хеш, репозиторій, клонувати); terms developers keep in Latin stay indeclinable: fetch, stash, pop, cherry-pick, revert, force-push, worktree, diff, upstream. Stage = додати до індексу, staged = в індексі, unstage = вилучити з індексу. Pull request = пул-реквест, review = рев’ю, features = Фічі, checked out = відкрито. States are impersonal participles (Закрито, Злито, Схвалено) and "by X" is "користувачем X" ("від X" after a noun like рев’ю). Durations are accusative after через (через 1 годину, 3 дні). Jira words follow developer usage: тікет, епік, реліз, версія виправлення. Compact ages: хв, год, дн, міс, р. Jira and the services take no case endings; gender: Jira is feminine (своєї Jira), but sentences use the present tense (Jira просить…) to avoid it.
notes.vi: Sentence case (only the first word capitalized), as in macOS's Vietnamese; the user is "bạn" (informal-neutral, like Apple), with "Hãy" for instructions. Git and Jira nouns that Vietnamese developers say in English stay English and never take a plural (commit, tag, remote, merge, rebase, cherry-pick, fetch, clone, stash, stage/unstage, pull request, review, ticket, epic, story, task, worktree, hash, upstream, HEAD, API token); everyday words are Vietnamese (nhánh, kho lưu trữ, tệp, thư mục, biểu đồ, thanh bên, tô sáng, hồ sơ, kiểm tra). "checked out" = "đã checkout"; "diverged" = "phân kỳ"; ahead/behind = "đi trước"/"đi sau". Drop (a stash) is "xóa" and Remove (a repository from the app, files untouched) is "gỡ bỏ". Jira's Done status is "hoàn thành" while the macOS Done button is "Xong". Compact ages use the shortest Vietnamese abbreviations (CLDR narrow): ph (phút), g (giờ), ng (ngày), th (tháng), n (năm). Timeline events put the actor first ("X đã merge").
notes.zh-Hans: Informal 你, as in Apple's Chinese. Mac words as macOS says them: 拷贝 (Copy), 存储 (Save), 好 (OK), 点按 (click), 边栏 (sidebar), 访达 (Finder), 终端 (Terminal), 钥匙串 (keychain), 载入/重新载入 (load/Reload), 应用程序 (Applications); app names in sentences get “ ” quotes. Git terms follow git's own zh_CN where it has one (获取 fetch, 贮藏 stash, 变基 rebase, 检出 checked out, 丢弃 drop, 还原 revert); cherry-pick is 拣选 and is written with the English once in the status lines (拣选（cherry-pick）). A pull request is 拉取请求 as in GitHub's Chinese docs. Jira words are what Jira shows in Chinese (史诗, 故事, 任务, 子任务, 修复版本, 待办, 进行中, 完成); a ticket is 工单 (not 问题, so Jira tickets stay apart from GitHub issues), its key 工单键. A merge commit is 合并提交; "live" epics (shipped) are 已上线. A term in commit messages ([Search]) is 关键词. A space between Chinese and Latin letters or digits, full-width punctuation, “ ” around names. Chinese has only the plural category 'other': plain strings, a measure word after numbers (个, 位 for people). Compact ages: 分钟, 小时, 天, 个月, 年.
notes.zh-Hant: Traditional Chinese as used in Taiwan, Apple's macOS wording (拷貝, 打開, 按一下, 檔案夾, 鑰匙圈, 終端機, 好 for OK). Informal 你, never 您. Full-width punctuation (，。：；？！（）、), 「」 for quotation marks and for names of other parts of the app, a space between Chinese and Latin letters or digits (「在 Finder 中顯示」, 「%lld 個提交」). git terms are translated with the Taiwan renderings (提交, 分支, 標籤, 合併, 重定基底, 揀選, 儲藏), except Pull Request, which stays English as Taiwanese developers write it. Jira terms follow Jira's Traditional Chinese (議題, 史詩, 修正版本). Counts take 個 (位 for people), no plural forms. Compact ages: %lld分, %lld時, %lld天, %lld個月, %@年. Working tree (the checked-out files) is 工作目錄, a linked worktree is 工作樹.
